summary: A shared $\Pi$-shaped Purcell filter integrated into the feedline provides broadband qubit protection in multiplexed circuit-QED via passive microwave interference between two open-ended stubs. For realistic parameters, the design achieves Purcell-limited relaxation times exceeding 1 ms over approximately 1.5 GHz while preserving dispersive readout.
motivation: Existing Purcell filters either require per-channel implementations (increasing overhead with processor size) or higher-order designs with multiple resonant sections (added complexity). A simple, shared filter that suppresses $\Re\{Y_\mathrm{env}(\omega)\}$ across the qubit band without degrading readout would enable scalable multiplexed architectures.
method: Two open-ended transmission-line stubs of lengths $\ell_+$ and $\ell_-$ are connected by an in-line section of length $\ell \approx (\ell_+ + \ell_-)/2$, forming a $\Pi$ network. The stubs' resonances at $\omega_\pm = \pi v/(2\ell_\pm)$ create overlapping suppression windows; destructive interference in the reflected field (setting $1 + L_1(\omega) \approx 0$ in the scattering picture) cancels radiative coupling to the external environment. SPICE and finite-element (HFSS) simulations verify performance for transmon-based architectures.
result: Simulations with realistic circuit parameters ($C_q = 81$ fF, $C_\mathrm{out} = 110$ fF, stub lengths $\ell_+ = 6.73$ mm and $\ell_- = 7.38$ mm) yield $T_P > 1$ ms over the target band [4.2, 4.5] GHz; four simultaneous qubits in a multiplexed readout architecture each achieve protection exceeding 1 ms within a 1.5 GHz window. Readout-mode frequency shift remains below 1 MHz, preserving compatibility with dispersive measurement.
